title: Release entry carries no YYYY-MM-DD date
why: Art. 17(2) of Directive (EU) 2024/2853 runs the 10-year longstop from the day that version was placed on the market. An undated heading cannot prove that day.

title: AS-IS / no-liability wording that Art. 15 voids
why: Art. 15 says liability towards an injured person may not be limited or excluded by a contractual provision. From 9 December 2026 the AS-IS clause stops doing the job it was written for.

title: Security fix with no CVE or GHSA identifier
why: Art. 11(2)(c) keeps a defect in your control when it turns on software updates you did or did not supply. Without an identifier you cannot show which defect a release removed.

title: Citation of the repealed 1985 Directive
why: Directive 85/374/EEC is repealed by Directive (EU) 2024/2853 with effect from 9 December 2026. A file that still cites it is describing a regime that has ended.

title: Product-liability date that is not 2026-12-09
why: Member States apply Directive (EU) 2024/2853 from 9 December 2026. Any other date on the same line is the single most copied mistake in generated text.

title: No dated support window anywhere in the file
why: Annex II(8) of the Cyber Resilience Act (EU) 2024/2847 requires the end date of the support period in the information given to users, and Art. 11(2)(c) PLD reads that window as your evidence.

title: No vulnerability-reporting contact
why: Annex II(2) CRA requires a single point of contact for reporting. Since 11 September 2026 an actively exploited vulnerability must reach ENISA within 24 hours.

title: Release heading names no version
why: Art. 4(1) treats each software version placed on the market as a product. 'Latest' and 'Current' identify no product.

title: Active-support claim older than the last dated release
why: A support claim that the release history does not back is the gap Art. 11(2)(c) opens: the update was in your control and it did not arrive.

title: Version withdrawn with no recorded reason
why: Art. 8 lets a court order you to disclose the record. A withdrawal with no reason on it leaves the defect unexplained in your own file.

title: Release dated after today
why: A product cannot be placed on the market in the future. The date decides the 10-year window under Art. 17(2), so a typo moves it.

title: 'Various fixes' with nothing named
why: Art. 10(2) lets a court presume defectiveness when ordered evidence is not produced. 'Various fixes' is not evidence of what was fixed.
